Playbook.name: Windows — UAC Bypass via Auto-Elevated LOLBin - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Privilege Escalation / Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An auto-elevating Windows binary (fodhelper, eventvwr, sdclt, computerdefaults, cmstp, wsreset, slui, changepk, dccw) spawned a shell/LOLBin - the signature of a UAC bypass to run code with elevated rights. Triage question: is this a UAC-bypass privilege escalation, or a rare benign auto-elevation?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: UAC bypass gives an attacker high-integrity (admin) execution from a medium-integrity foothold without a prompt.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the auto-elevated-binary child is a UAC bypass or benign.

Step.name: Which auto-elevated binary spawned what
Step.Purpose: The parent (fodhelper/eventvwr/etc.) and the child command reveal the bypass and its payload.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.parent.name RLIKE "(?i)(fodhelper|eventvwr|sdclt|computerdefaults|cmstp|wsreset|slui|changepk|dccw).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: fodhelper.exe or eventvwr.exe spawning cmd/powershell is a textbook UAC bypass (these binaries do not normally spawn shells). The child command shows what the attacker elevated to run.

Step.name: Process origin and account on the host
Step.Purpose: The parent process and account reveal whether this was interactive attacker activity or an automated/service context.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A suspicious process spawned by an office app/browser/script interpreter, run by a normal user, is more concerning than one under a known admin/automation parent.

Node.Condition: An auto-elevated binary spawning a shell/LOLBin (fodhelper/eventvwr -> cmd/powershell).
Node.Result: True Positive (UAC Bypass / Privilege Escalation - IR)

Node.Condition: A rare, explainable benign auto-elevation confirmed harmless on inspection.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-UAC-CHILD, INV-02-PROC-TREE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify on the host; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: A UAC bypass for privilege escalation.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; open IR; the account is likely compromised at medium integrity.
Hunt the foothold origin and what ran elevated.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A software installer triggering auto-elevation legitimately.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
